source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information/detail and compare FRU data with `ipmitool fru print`.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes a single `/Chassis/FRU_FAN` resource and extracts only Manufacturer, ProductName and SerialNumber. It does not execute the required IPMI comparison, establish how many fan FRUs exist or how a FRU maps to fan tray/module/rotors, distinguish Board from Product field namespaces, preserve custom fields or protect identifiers.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly restores complete fan-FRU topology and protected Redfish/IPMI/WebUI parity while separating static identity from live fan health, but leaves the finite Project FRU map and expected asset fields as Pending.

old_problem: A three-field response from one guessed chassis URI can falsely represent a tray-level record as every physical fan, overlook multiple FRU devices, compare the wrong IPMI FRU ID, or collapse Board and Product serial/part fields. The previous review identified these correctness risks but retained Pending for the Project fan-assembly and FRU-device map.
disposition_reason: Discover every actual fan-related chassis/assembly resource and enumerate IPMI FRU devices, then use the approved cooling topology to bind each FRU record to its fan tray/module/assembly and covered rotor set. Compare all required Chassis, Board, Product, multi-record and custom fields by their true namespace across Redfish, IPMI and actual WebUI, with protected serial tokens. The cardinality/map and asset baseline are versioned Project inputs and do not require a new design decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 974, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 975 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 975 / variant ff42274ee1631686.

The IPMI Platform Management FRU Information Storage Definition separates Common Header, Internal Use, Chassis, Board, Product and MultiRecord areas and defines typed/length-encoded fields. Values from different areas with similar names are not interchangeable.

DMTF Chassis, Assembly and Fan relationships can expose persistent fan assembly identity, but a vendor resource name `FRU_FAN` and its granularity are OEM/Project facts that must be discovered and mapped rather than guessed.

Static FRU manufacturer/part/serial data proves asset identity, not current rotor speed, fan presence signal, health or airflow. The separate `_F`/`_R` telemetry cases remain independent and cannot be declared passed by this record.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-08, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require exact identity, no OEM guessing, actual WebUI evidence and independent coverage; ED-33 through ED-38 allow Project parameterization and prohibit log clear, FRU write, fan action, reset/power and retry.

test_case.test_name: Validate every FRU_FAN record's assembly scope and complete Redfish/IPMI/WebUI identity parity
test_case.purpose: Verify every Project-defined fan FRU device or assembly is present exactly once, bound to the correct fan tray/module/slot and covered rotor/channel set, and exposes complete correct persistent asset data consistently through read-only IPMI FRU decoding, discovered Redfish resources and the actual BMC WebUI, without treating FRU identity as live fan-health proof.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/chassis/cooling/WebUI identity and approved fan tray/module/assembly/slot/rotor topology
Authoritative FRU_FAN cardinality and granularity stating which physical fan modules or rotor channels each FRU device/resource covers
Approved mapping among IPMI FRU device ID/description, Redfish Chassis/Assembly/member URI and WebUI entry for every fan FRU
Versioned expected asset baseline by FRU area/field: Chassis, Board, Product, MultiRecord and required custom fields, encodings, blank/unsupported rules and manufacture date where applicable
Read-only IPMI FRU decoder/version and DMTF-schema-aware protected Redfish client using discovered resources rather than a fixed `FRU_FAN` URI
Actual rendered WebUI detail mapping, trusted TLS/IPMI sessions, protected credentials, serial/asset tokenization, preserved logs and evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and capture BMC/decoder versions. Enumerate the Chassis collection and advertised Assembly/Fan relationships to locate all fan-related FRU resources; do not assume `/Chassis/FRU_FAN` or one resource. Enumerate read-only `ipmitool fru print` output with FRU device descriptions/IDs, select each fan FRU only through the approved map, and preserve complete redacted output. For every expected FRU, bind its IPMI ID and Redfish/WebUI resource to the physical tray/module/assembly/slot and covered rotor/channel set. Compare each required field within its exact IPMI namespace—Chassis type/part/serial, Board manufacture time/manufacturer/product/serial/part/file ID, Product manufacturer/name/part/version/serial/asset tag/file ID, MultiRecord/custom fields—and its explicitly mapped Redfish/WebUI semantic; retain missing, blank, unsupported and duplicate values distinctly. Capture the actual rendered WebUI Chassis/fan FRU list and every required detail. Use protected stable tokens for serial/asset correlation. Preserve pre/post SEL/audit evidence. Do not clear logs, write/edit FRU, toggle an indicator, change PWM/thresholds, disconnect/reseat fans, inject faults, reset/reboot or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected fan FRU device/assembly appears exactly once with an unambiguous physical scope and identical approved persistent identity across the mapped IPMI areas, Redfish fields and actual WebUI after normalization. Board and Product fields remain distinct, custom/MultiRecord/blank/unsupported semantics match the baseline, protected identifiers correlate without disclosure, and no extra/missing/duplicate/swapped assembly exists. Live fan status is explicitly not inferred, and fan/FRU/system state remains unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete expected FRU cardinality, topology and interface mapping; full required IPMI area/field preservation; field-specific Redfish/IPMI/WebUI/baseline parity; actual rendered WebUI detail; and protected stable identity. One guessed endpoint, three strings, one tray record counted as multiple fans, aggregate fan status or telemetry borrowed from another case cannot pass. Missing/extra/duplicate/ambiguous FRU, wrong assembly scope/IPMI ID, Board/Product namespace substitution, field/encoding/reference mismatch or UI/API/IPMI disagreement is FAIL. Missing topology, granularity, interface map or expected baseline is NOT READY rather than Pending, and no OEM URI/field is invented.
safety_gate: Use only certificate-verified Redfish reads and read-only IPMI FRU print operations with protected credentials; discover resources and FRU IDs before selecting evidence.
Map FRU devices to fan trays/modules/assemblies and rotor/channel coverage through the approved topology; never assume one FRU per physical rotor or one aggregate FRU covers every fan.
Keep Chassis, Board, Product, MultiRecord and custom-field namespaces distinct and protect serial/asset identifiers with stable tokens in shared evidence.
Static FRU identity must not be used as proof of RPM, airflow, presence sensor or live health; those separate source variants retain independent evidence.
Preserve logs; prohibit FRU write/edit, fan PWM/threshold/override change, LED actuation, disconnect/reseat, fault injection, reset/reboot and power transitions.
Stop on unknown FRU ID, ambiguous physical scope, parse/checksum concern or cross-interface mismatch and do not auto-retry through reset or power.
expected_evidence: Immutable target, Redfish schema and IPMI decoder identity plus approved fan FRU cardinality/granularity and assembly/slot/rotor topology
Complete redacted Chassis/Assembly/Fan resource artifacts and full read-only IPMI FRU print output with device IDs/descriptions, timestamps and hashes
Per-FRU mapping table joining physical assembly scope, IPMI device, Redfish member and WebUI entry without collapsing multiple rotor/channel identities
Field-by-field Chassis/Board/Product/MultiRecord/custom parity matrix with expected values, normalization, protected tokens and verdicts
Actual rendered WebUI Chassis/fan FRU table and detail visual artifacts with Redfish/IPMI/reference comparison
Preserved pre/post logs, no-write/no-control/no-reset/no-power proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On unknown cardinality, ambiguous FRU-to-assembly scope, parse/checksum issue or field mismatch, stop and preserve/redact the complete IPMI, Redfish, WebUI and log evidence for the cooling/asset owner. Do not clear logs, edit FRU, actuate indicators, manipulate/disconnect fans, inject faults, reset/reboot, power-cycle or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: The Master consistently requests fan FRU content and explicit WebUI/IPMI comparison. Missing cardinality and incomplete DeepSeek fields are implementation gaps, not conflicting source purposes.

blocked.reason: Static fan-FRU identity/parity is standard and technically defined. FRU granularity, physical/interface mapping and expected asset data are bounded Project configuration inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Fan FRU cardinality/granularity; tray/module/assembly/slot/rotor topology; IPMI ID↔Redfish↔WebUI map; expected per-area/custom fields and encoding rules; trust, redaction and freshness policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY FAN FRU PARITY REVIEW ONLY; NO REDFISH, IPMI, WEBUI, LOG CLEAR, FRU WRITE, FAN/LED, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
